subject.title: [Feature Request] Telegram Channel: Support Thread Binding for Subagent Sessions

question: Should Telegram expose child-topic native subagent session spawning now, and if so should it use a per-kind capability while preserving Telegram's default current-conversation placement?
rationale: Current main has core binding primitives and Telegram adapter capability, but creating user-visible child topics for subagent sessions affects chat UX, plugin/API shape, and message/session routing defaults.

options.title: Review the active Telegram candidate
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82023 as the main design input, require a rebase onto the core session-binding path, and demand final-head live Telegram proof before merge.

options.title: Keep current-conversation binding only
options.body: Document that Telegram supports persistent binding only to the current conversation/topic for now and leave child-topic subagent spawning deferred.

options.title: Reject child-topic subagent spawning
options.body: Close this feature direction and associated candidate PRs if maintainers decide internal subagent work should not create Telegram topics.

recommendation.title: Review the active Telegram candidate
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82023 as the main design input, require a rebase onto the core session-binding path, and demand final-head live Telegram proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the merged core session-binding refactor that now defines the correct implementation layer for this feature.
